summary: Round 2's fix RELOCATED the defect. It clamped the single star list that detect_stars_with_stats returns to SELECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY (0.7) for every caller — including callers that had deliberately passed a WIDER ceiling because they are measuring the field, not picking stars to work with. The casualty is the entire Dart science pipeline (DefaultScienceBackend.measureStars explicitly asks for 0.95 and was silently given 0.7), and through it the PSF field map, whose medianEccentricity is what FrameAutoGrader grades frames on. So the original round-1 defect — a threshold clipped at the measurement ceiling, therefore un-fireable — came back one level up, on the PERSISTED grading path. Round 3 splits the third population out: StarDetectionResult now carries `sources`, the caller's own ceiling honoured verbatim, alongside `stars` (the working set, still clamped so the guider/autofocus fix from round 2 is untouched). Landing the fix end-to-end needs one 2-line change in bridge/src/api/imaging.rs, which is outside this item's ownership.

point_1_named_consumers.instructions.rs:4793 (autofocus HFR): calculate_hfr_with_crops calls detect_stars_with_stats(&imaging_data, &StarDetectionConfig::default()) and filters result.stars by the crop window. Selection-filtered. No edit needed.
point_1_named_consumers.platesolve.rs:1738: NOT A DEFECT — inside `#[cfg(test)] fn extract_plate_stars` (attribute at platesolve.rs:1701). Does not exist in a release build.
point_1_named_consumers.background_extraction.rs:973: CORRECTLY LEFT LOOSE — that config builds a STAR MASK. A trailed star covers MORE pixels and must be masked too; tightening it would leave trails unmasked for the background model to fit.

point_2_dart_agreement.verdict: CORRECT as of round 2, and proved load-bearing by revert, not just by reading.
point_2_dart_agreement.revert_proof: Deleted `if (img.starCount == 0) return 'Auto-grade: $_unmeasurableFrameReason';` from gradeFrame -> 4 tests FAILED, including the end-to-end 'FrameAutoGrader end-to-end a starless light is persisted as rejected, not accepted' which drives the real FrameAutoGrader against a real in-memory SkotiqDatabase and asserts the PERSISTED is_accepted. Restored byte-identical -> 8/8 pass.
point_2_dart_agreement.cross_engine_check: Walked grade_frame (image_grading.rs:164-260) against gradeFrame/gradeStats field by field. is_active/isEmpty early-out, Some(0)/==0 zero-star reject, absolute HFR, eccentricity and star-count floor all agree. Rust returns on the first failure and Dart collects all reasons — cosmetic. Rust's hfr_baseline_percent and Dart's maxGuidingRmsTotalArcsec have no counterpart on the other side, but they are separate configured features, not the same rule diverging.
point_2_dart_agreement.star_count_provenance_check: Both engines compare the SAME number. Native FrameMetrics.star_count comes from detect_stars_in_image (permissive detect_stars, unified_device_ops.rs:1699). Dart ImageStats.starCount comes from api/imaging.rs:1067 (also permissive detect_stars), and captured_images.star_count is stamped from it (imaging_service/persistence.dart:161). Round 2's change of StarDetectionResult.star_count to the *usable* count does NOT leak onto either grading path.

point_3_consecutive_rejects.verdict: ANSWERED, and the answer re-checked. An unmeasurable frame SHOULD count.
point_3_consecutive_rejects.why: Three lights in a row with zero stars is not a marginal quality dip that stacking absorbs — it is clouds, a dust cap, or a slew that missed, and it will ruin every remaining exposure until someone intervenes. The failure worth avoiding is the SILENT one: hours of empty subs on disk while the run reports healthy. Pause is recoverable; it does not abort the sequence or discard the target.
point_3_consecutive_rejects.where_the_comment_lives: The _unmeasurableFrameReason doc comment in frame_grade_rules.dart, which also states plainly that the escalation lives entirely on the native side (instructions.rs:3163 increments on every FrameGrade::Reject regardless of reason; executor/mod.rs:2089 escalates to an operator pause) so the Dart engine cannot itself pause a run. image_grading.rs is not in this item's ownership, so the Rust-side comment is listed under needs_shared_change as a P3.

the_defect_round_2_introduced.mechanism: detect_stars_with_stats returned exactly ONE star list. Round 2 narrowed it to min(config.max_eccentricity, SELECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY). api_detect_stars_in_file (bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:2467) hands that list straight back as the API's `stars`.
the_defect_round_2_introduced.the_caller_that_was_steamrolled: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/default_science_backend.dart:107-117 — DefaultScienceBackend.measureStars builds StarDetectionConfigApi(detectionSigma: 4.0, minArea: 4, maxArea: 1024, maxEccentricity: 0.95, hfrRadius: 6, minHfr: 0.6, minSnr: 4.0, maxSharpness: 100.0). It asks for 0.95 ON PURPOSE and got 0.7.
the_defect_round_2_introduced.blast_radius: measureStars is the single entry point for computePsfFieldMap (:452), photometric zero-point calibration (:180), astrometric residuals (:535) and tracking-drift analysis (:602/:606/:650), plus science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:155.
the_defect_round_2_introduced.worst_consequence: PsfTileMetric.medianEccentricity (and roundness = 1 - ecc) was capped at 0.7, and FrameAutoGrader sources its eccentricity from exactly those tiles (frame_auto_grader.dart:46-48). A FrameGradeRules.maxEccentricity above 0.7 therefore became un-fireable on the persisted auto-grading path — the round-1 defect verbatim. On a fully trailed frame it is worse than a cap: every tile ends up with starCount 0, _psfFieldMetrics returns null, the eccentricity rule is skipped for 'lack of evidence', and gradeFrame ACCEPTS — while the live badge, which reads the honest ImageStats.eccentricity measured over the permissive population, REJECTS. That is the badge-vs-disk contradiction this item was opened for, alive in the one code path round 2 declared closed.
the_defect_round_2_introduced.proof_it_is_a_regression_not_pre_existin: `git show HEAD:native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs` line 1032: `let stars = detect_stars(image, config);` — the caller's ceiling, unclipped, both before round 1 and after it. Round 2 is the sole cause.

changes_this_round.what: StarDetectionResult gains `pub sources: Vec<DetectedStar>` — every source that passed the CALLER'S OWN config, unnarrowed by the working-star ceiling. detect_stars_with_stats now derives three populations from its single detection pass instead of two, and the struct carries a table documenting which question each answers: `stars` at min(config, 0.7) = 'what can I work with'; `sources` at config.max_eccentricity = 'what did I ask for'; detected_star_count / median_eccentricity at max(config, 0.95) = 'what is in this frame'.
changes_this_round.why_stars_is_still_clamped: Because the guider, autofocus and frame weighting all pass StarDetectionConfig::default(), whose max_eccentricity IS 0.95 — numerically identical to what measureStars passes. One f64 cannot carry the caller's intent, so `stars` keeps the safe answer and `sources` carries the caller's verbatim one. selection_eccentricity_ceiling's doc now says this outright instead of claiming the caller's choice is always kept.
changes_this_round.build_safety: Purely additive. No StarDetectionResult struct literal exists anywhere outside stats.rs, so nothing else needed touching; `cargo check -p skotiq_bridge --lib` is clean.

changes_this_round.what: Doc-only. gradeFrame's contract comment previously read 'Both production callers (FrameAutoGrader and the Image Grader dialog) source them from the frame's PSF field-map tiles' — i.e. it documented the wrong data source as if it were the contract. Replaced with what [eccentricity] must actually be: captured_images.eccentricity, the per-frame median the native grader graded on, stamped from ImageStats.eccentricity by imaging_service/persistence.dart:189-195 (and described by images_dao.dart:580 as 'mirrors the Rust grader's median star eccentricity').
changes_this_round.why_no_behaviour_change_here: The rule engine is correct and its zero-star rule is load-bearing (proved by revert). The Dart-side defect is that both gradeFrame callers feed it a PSF-tile aggregate when the exact number the native grader used is already on the row. Fixing that means editing frame_auto_grader.dart / image_grader_dialog.dart / images_dao.dart, none of which are in this item's ownership.

added: imaging/src/stats.rs::a_caller_that_widened_the_ceiling_to_measure_the_field_still_gets_its_stars — drives detect_stars_with_stats from rendered pixels with science_pipeline_config(), a field-for-field reproduction of what api_detect_stars_in_file builds from the StarDetectionConfigApi that DefaultScienceBackend.measureStars sends (including the default PhotometryOptions apertureRadiusPixels: 6 / minSnr: 4.0). Asserts sources keeps the trailed stars, sources never exceeds the caller's ceiling, stars stays round, and the two populations actually differ on the frame.

imaging/src/stats.rs::sources_honours_a_caller_that_asked_for_a_tight_ceiling — the other direction, using the FITS analysis screen's 0.7 config: sources must NOT receive the widened measurement population, while detected_star_count still shows the smears were measured for the shape statistic.

revert_proof.line_reverted: detect_stars_with_stats: `sources.retain(|s| s.eccentricity <= config.max_eccentricity);` -> `sources.retain(|s| s.eccentricity <= selection_eccentricity_ceiling(config));` — i.e. exactly round 2's behaviour, where the only list handed back is the selection-clamped one.
revert_proof.result: 1 FAILED: a_caller_that_widened_the_ceiling_to_measure_the_field_still_gets_its_stars, panicked at stats.rs:2092 'a caller asking for e <= 0.95 must get the trailed sources back; got 8 sources, max ecc 0.0'. Every trailed source silently discarded, exactly as the science pipeline experiences it today. Restored from a byte-identical copy -> 28/28 stats tests pass.

4 FAILED, including the wiring test 'FrameAutoGrader end-to-end a starless light is persisted as rejected, not accepted' (drives the real FrameAutoGrader.gradeCapturedFrame against a real in-memory SkotiqDatabase and asserts the persisted is_accepted). Restored byte-identical (verified with diff) -> 8/8 pass. This was run to confirm round 2's Dart fix is genuinely load-bearing rather than merely present.

They render elliptical-Gaussian pixels, call the production function detect_stars_with_stats, and pass the exact config the production Dart caller sends through the bridge. The Dart revert test goes through FrameAutoGrader + a real database, so cutting the production call site fails it.

needs_shared_change: P1 / bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:2467-2468 and :2492 — `api_detect_stars_in_file` must hand back the population the caller asked for, not the working set. Change `let stars: Vec<DetectedStarInfo> = result.stars.iter()` to `result.sources.iter()`, and `star_count: result.star_count` to `star_count: result.sources.len() as u32`. THIS IS THE ONE CHANGE THAT MAKES ROUND 3 LIVE. Correct for both of that API's Dart callers: DefaultScienceBackend.measureStars asked for 0.95 and gets 0.95 (restoring the PSF field map, photometry, astrometric residuals and the FrameAutoGrader eccentricity gate); the FITS star-analysis screen asked for 0.7 and still gets 0.7, because `sources` is the caller's ceiling verbatim. Leave median_hfr / median_fwhm / median_snr on `result.*` — those are correctly computed over the working set — and leave median_eccentricity alone, it is already measured over the widened population.

P1 / bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs:1659 `calculate_image_hfr` and bridge/src/real_device_ops.rs:2989 `calculate_image_hfr` (and bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs:1307 if it carries the same body) — both compute a MEAN HFR over `detect_stars(&img, &StarDetectionConfig::default())`, i.e. the permissive 0.95 population. This is the per-frame HFR the sequencer's capture loop consumes at instructions.rs:2184, and it feeds (a) FrameMetrics.hfr -> the absolute and baseline-relative HFR reject gates and (b) hfr_values -> the HfrDegraded / FocusDrift triggers. A wind-trailed frame therefore reads as focus drift, and the sequencer answers focus drift by burning exposures on an autofocus run that cannot fix trailing. This was disclosed by round 2 and not fixed; it is still the single largest remaining piece of the 0.7 -> 0.95 blast radius. Fix in each: replace the whole body with `Ok(skotiq_imaging::calculate_median_hfr(&img))` — that public helper already takes only an image, builds StarDetectionConfig::default() itself, uses detect_stars_for_selection, takes a MEDIAN of the brightest 50% and filters 0 < hfr < 20. It also fixes the second, separate bug in those functions (a mean, which a single blended or saturated detection skews). Leave `detect_stars_in_image` and `measure_frame_eccentricity` in both files on the permissive `detect_stars` — those two want the measurement population and are correct as-is.

P1 / packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/frame_auto_grader.dart:39-50 + a new `getEccentricity(int imageId)` on packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/images_dao.dart (alongside the existing getFwhm at :542) — FrameAutoGrader sources eccentricity from PSF field-map tiles when the exact number the native grader graded on is already on the row. captured_images.eccentricity is stamped from ImageStats.eccentricity by imaging_service/persistence.dart:189-195, and images_dao.dart:580 already documents it as 'mirrors the Rust grader's median star eccentricity'. Prefer the row; fall back to the PSF tiles only when the column is null, exactly as the code already does for FWHM. Without this the persisted auto-grade and the live SubQualityBadge grade the same frame off two different eccentricity measurements, and the PSF one is absent whenever the science stage did not run. Same change applies to packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/image_grader_dialog.dart:249.

P2 / bridge/src/imaging_ops.rs:636 `ImagingSession::calculate_hfr_avg` — same mean-over-permissive-population defect on the interactive imaging-session HFR readout (called from :117 and :212). Replace the body with `skotiq_imaging::calculate_median_hfr(image).unwrap_or(0.0)`.

P2 / bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1067-1110 (unified display path) — computes star_count, median HFR and median FWHM inline from `detect_stars(&image, &default())`. star_count is CORRECT on the permissive population (it is what the zero-star grading rule keys on and what captured_images.star_count is stamped from — do not change it), and median_eccentricity via frame_eccentricity is correct. But the HFR and FWHM medians should come from `detect_stars_for_selection`, or the whole block replaced by a single `detect_stars_with_stats` call which now returns star_count, sources, detected_star_count, the selection-filtered medians and an unclipped median_eccentricity in one pass.

P3 / bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:2428 `StarDetectionConfigApi::default().max_eccentricity = 0.7` — not a correctness bug (the measurement pass inside detect_stars_with_stats is widened, so median_eccentricity is honest), but the field reads as a detection ceiling and behaves as a selection ceiling. Suggest `skotiq_imaging::SELECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY` with a comment.

P3 / sequencer/src/quality/image_grading.rs — the module doc explains the zero-star rule but not why an unmeasurable frame is allowed to count toward max_consecutive_rejects. Copy the reasoning from FrameGradeRules._unmeasurableFrameReason so it sits next to the code that actually escalates.

P3 / bridge/src/builtin_guider.rs:1402 — when summary.stars is empty the guider reports no lock star. It could read summary.detected_star_count to say 'stars present but all trailed — check the mount' instead of implying 'no stars — check for clouds'. Behaviour without this is correct, just less specific.

NOT NEEDED, assessed: imaging/src/platesolve.rs (cfg(test) only), imaging/src/background_extraction.rs (star masking wants trails masked), imaging/src/frame_weighting.rs (star_count/median_fwhm over the working set is the right weighting signal, and fwhm_ratio already treats fwhm == 0 as worst-possible focus rather than perfect), imaging/src/deconvolution.rs (its own max_eccentricity: 0.5 is honoured because it calls detect_stars directly), imaging/src/star_reduction.rs and imaging/src/registration.rs (their explicit max_eccentricity: 1.0 configs also go through detect_stars directly).
caveats: OUTCOME IS PARTIAL BY DESIGN, NOT BY OMISSION: `sources` is inert until bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:2467/:2492 reads it. That file is outside this item's ownership and other agents are running concurrently. I could not fix it from stats.rs alone — I traced every alternative and none works: StarDetectionConfig::default().max_eccentricity must stay 0.95 because measure_frame_eccentricity and detect_stars_in_image call detect_stars(default) directly for the grading metrics, and it is numerically identical to what measureStars passes, so the intent simply is not present in the config. Adding a second field to StarDetectionConfig would break the full struct literal at api/imaging.rs:2447 and therefore the bridge build. The additive field is the largest correct change that cannot break a concurrent agent.

Behaviour change from round 2 that is now documented rather than silent: on a night where every star is trailed past e=0.7 the built-in guider declines to lock rather than chase a smear, and calculate_median_hfr returns None instead of an inflated number. Both are restorations of pre-0.95 behaviour.
Validated on synthetic elliptical-Gaussian fields only — not against a real trailed sub from a telescope.
detected_star_count and now sources are public fields with no production consumer until the P1 bridge change lands.
